verdict:
Not at fern level yet. Mean 6.25, a small step up from round 7 (6.13). The gain is all in seated_called. Dawn no longer stares into the lens. Her face now turns about 30 degrees past it, to screen left, and her left hand has moved from her lap to the front of the aisle armrest. The case holds its place across the cut. From seated to seated_called its centre moves from about (695,490) to (686,468), which is just what the zoom from 52 to 44 mm about the frame centre does.

The beat still reads as a statue looking up at the ceiling, not a woman hearing her flight called. The head is aimed at the PA disc on the ceiling, about 11 m away and about 14 degrees above level. The camera sits just below her eyes and sees under her jaw, so the lift looks bigger than it is. The torso stays upright against the backrest and the feet do not move. The left arm hangs nearly straight, and the hand rests on the pad instead of pushing on it.

Seated, wide and window are almost unchanged from the last round: 1,883, 803 and 1,269 pixels changed by more than 25 levels, and in wide and window those changes are on Dawn. Their layout is sound. The graded peaks of wide and window are 213 and 225, so nothing goes above 250.

Remaining faults:
- The blank gate panels look like grey cards, not lit screens.
- The curtain wall barely reads as glass. The only reflections are two faint ghosts of ceiling fittings in the window sky, about 6 levels above their surroundings.
- The aircraft is a smooth satin model with no surface detail.
- Dawn's bun is a flat spiral that reads from behind as a snail shell or an ear. Her crown sits under the downlight and renders brighter than her neck, so the head reads as bald.
- The empty seat beside her in seated and seated_called is a lit grey slab, brighter than the rows behind (about 62 and 69 against 38 to 43).

The Chapter 4 title is clear of her. In the rendered 04-01 shot, the "04 - Yes" block ends at about x 315 on the 1920 frame and her head starts at about x 555, so about 240 px separate them, even at the end of the 4 % push.
answers:
1) Do Dawn's eyeline and armrest brace make the boarding call read? Partly.

The eyeline is fixed in one way. It now goes past the lens, about 29 degrees off axis to screen left, as round 7 asked. But brace_for_call aims the head at GATE_SPEAKER (9.6, 5.94, 3.894), a disc on the ceiling, and it also tips the neck back 6 degrees (_turn neck -6, -22). Her chin lifts, and the visible neck is clearly longer than in seated, where the head is tipped 14 degrees down. The yaw toward the speaker is about 74 degrees to her right, much the same as toward the door. What lifts the face is the pitch: about 14 degrees up, seen from a camera at 1.10 m that looks under her jaw. The face is nearly three-quarter and tipped toward the ceiling, and it reads as rapture, not alertness. People hearing a gate call look at the gate: the podium, the door and its sign. They do not look at the speaker.

The brace does not read as one:
- The left arm hangs almost straight to the front end of the pad, and the fingers drape over the end.
- The shoulder does not rise, the torso does not lean forward and the feet do not draw back, so nothing shows her weight moving toward standing.
- Her right hand still lies limp on her thigh.

Without the PA sound the frame says "she looked up". With the sound it says "she heard something". It does not yet say "that is my flight".

2) Does the case stay in place across the cut? Yes. Seated and seated_called share the camera position and aim; only the lens changes, from 52 to 44 mm. The case's centre moves from about (695,490) to (686,468) on the 1280 frame. That is what the zoom about (640,360) predicts: (686,470). Its wheels, its contact shadow and its gap to her shoe are the same in both. In wide and window the case stands in the aisle at her left, which matches. Continuity holds.

3) Your graded medians of 24.0 and 25.2 are the case-body medians across the cut (your 8fb9078 note), not medians of whole frames. On the case body (seated x 630-760, y 410-600; seated_called x 632-742, y 400-570) I measure 25 graded in both. That agrees with your figures within the choice of box, so the case keeps its dark charcoal value across the cut.

For the whole frames of wide and window:
- Graded medians are 23.0 and 25.0 (Rec.601).
- Maxima are 213 and 225 in luma, and 218 and 229 in the brightest single channel, so nothing is above 250.
- The raw PNGs clip only at point sources, which is acceptable. Wide has 38 pixels at 250 or more: the distant apron lights at the top left and three small points right of the door sign. Window has 533: the mast lamp heads along the top edge and a few taxi lights.
- Wide has 8.9 % of graded pixels below 8, the most in the stage (window 3.7 %, the two seated frames under 1 %).

The crush in the wide sits in the corners, measured as quarter-width by quarter-height boxes:
- 27 % in the top left: the sky above the aircraft.
- 24 % in the bottom right and 20 % in the bottom left: the foreground seat rows.

AGENT_BRIEF.md says to avoid areas the grade crushes to pure black when they carry the place (windows, the far wall). The top-left corner is window.

4) The apron through the glass reads. It shows the airliner nose-in, both engines, the wing, the baggage carts, the taxi lights in bokeh, the two flood masts and the jet bridge. The window shot has the best composition in the stage. But the aircraft reads as a model:
- The fuselage has one broad, soft highlight on the upper left of the crown (about 150-160 graded, peak 188) that rolls off to about 35-45 toward the nose. That is a diffuse satin roll-off, with no crisp specular streak from the floods.
- No panel lines or door outlines read at this distance, apart from the cockpit glazing and the band of cabin windows. The shader has them, but they are too faint.
- The wing tapers in thickness but is a flat-faced slab with square edges, so it reads as a plank.
- The covered baggage carts read as plain boxes.

Above all, the glass hardly exists on screen. Its only reflections are two ghosts of ceiling fittings in the sky (around x 245-290, y 100 and x 665-700, y 113), about 6 levels above the sky and visible only when the shadows are lifted. There is no reflection of the lit pool or of Dawn. At night, with a lit interior, that reflection is how glass reads. In the window shot it would also be a free storytelling image: her faint reflected face and front over the aircraft.

5) The blank gate panels have no lettering, which is good. But they do not glow. In the wide:
- the gate sign face is about 110 graded (peak 116)
- the podium screen is about 116 (peak 121)
- the floor-standing sign is about 101 (peak 106).

That is the value of the lit apron behind the glass (median about 101 under the jet bridge), so they read as grey cards or whiteboards, not backlit panels. Their bezels are dark (about 12), which is right. There is no distinct pool on the podium top or the carpet in front of them (median about 49). Three small clipped points to the right of the door sign (raw about x 1080, 1087 and 1132, y 94) read as stray dots at this size. They are probably the jet bridge's service lamps seen through the glass, so check what they are before removing them.

6) The floor reflections:
- The carpet is correctly matte. The tile grid and the quarter-turned rib carry it, and there should be no mirror reflections on carpet.
- The stone strip along the glass shows a soft sheen in the wide (about 70, peak 213 at x 539, y 365, the brightest pixel in the frame), which is plausible.
- In window, the floor gets brighter toward the camera: about 38 at the glass, about 55 around the case and at the bottom centre. That is the opposite of what a contre-jour silhouette needs. The eye drops to the near floor instead of staying on her against the apron.

fixes.problem: The head lifts toward the ceiling PA disc about 11 m away (about 14 degrees up, with the neck tipped back 6 degrees), so the beat reads as a gaze at the sky, not as hearing the boarding call.
fixes.fix: In departure_gate.py brace_for_call, aim the head at the gate door instead of GATE_SPEAKER: look = Vector((st.DOOR_X, st.WIN - 0.1, 1.9)) - (world @ head.head). The door is at nearly the same bearing as the speaker (about 73 degrees to her right against 74), so her turn of about 29 degrees past the lens is kept and only the pitch drops, from about 14 degrees to about 4. Change the neck turn from _turn(rig, 'neck', -6, -22) to (0, -22) so the neck no longer tips back, and cap head pitch at 8 degrees above level. Check from the seated camera that the face reads as a three-quarter view turned to screen left with the chin level and the underside of the jaw not showing.

fixes.problem: The brace is passive: a nearly straight arm, the hand draped over the end of the pad, an upright torso and unchanged feet. Nothing says she is about to stand.
fixes.fix:
Make these changes in brace_for_call:
- Chest: _turn(rig, 'chest', 9, -6) instead of (0, -6), so the shoulders come about 5-8 cm off the backrest.
- Left hand: move the target 4 cm back and 1 cm down, Vector((pad_x + 0.001, ROW_Y - 0.006, 0.667)), so the elbow bends 20-30 degrees with the elbow out to the side. Flatten the fingers onto the pad (knuckle curls about 10, 6, 4) and extend the wrist 25-30 degrees so the heel of the hand presses. Move the 'called hand flag' back about 4 cm with it; its y range now starts at ROW_Y + 0.039 and would miss the wrist.
- Feet: draw both back 6-8 cm by making the shin angle about 10 degrees smaller than the solved value. In sit_legs the shin angle is the forward swing from vertical, so a larger value moves the feet forward. Re-solve so the soles stay on the carpet.
- Right hand: lift it off the thigh onto the front of the right-hand armrest (the shared one at ARM_X[1]) or onto the seat edge beside her thigh. The case is on her left, out of this hand's reach.
- Reset: add every bone you newly pose (thigh_fk, shin_fk and foot_fk on both sides, any spine bone, the right hand) to CALL_CONTROLS, so the other cameras reset to the seated pose.
- Check: the face must stay brighter than both hands.

fixes.problem: The gate sign face (about 110 graded), the podium screen (about 116) and the floor sign (about 101) sit at the value of the lit apron behind the glass. They look like grey cards and throw no visible spill.
fixes.fix: In departure_gate_mats.py raise the emitters: sign 1.6 to about 4.0, sign_mid 0.9 to about 2.6, screen_front 1.1 to about 2.6, keeping the falloff so the edges stay dimmer. In departure_gate_set.py raise gate_sign_light from 26 to about 60 W and fsign_glow from 1.5 to about 6 W. Add a 0.5 x 0.3 m area light about 0.25 m in front of each podium screen at about 5 W, so a cool pool shows on the podium top and the carpet. Target faces of about 150-180 graded, with the bezels (sign_case, now about 12) under 40 and everything under 250. The three small clipped points to the right of the door sign (raw about x 1080, 1087 and 1132, y 94) are probably the jet bridge's service lamps through the glass. Confirm what they are before removing anything. If they are designed lamps, bring them below clipping, or give them enough size or housing to read as lamps rather than dust.

fixes.problem: Dawn's bun is a flat spiral coil (1.56 turns, almost no depth) that reads from behind as a snail shell or an ear. Under the downlight her crown renders brighter than her neck (about 86 against 65 graded), so the head reads as bald.
fixes.fix: In dawn(), replace the flat coil with a solid low bun: an ellipsoid of about 0.075 x 0.05 x 0.055 m standing 3.5-4 cm out from the nape, plus a torus wrap (major radius 0.03, minor radius 0.012) twisted 20 degrees around it, keeping the existing ring-wave bump. Do not retint the hair. It is already 0.4 of the stone in the shared cast (HAIR 0.2 against STONE 0.5 in noir-kit/cast.py), and a value set per stage would break the one character system in DECISIONS.md. It renders bright because the fitting sits almost straight above her crown. For the window camera only, add a small camera-invisible flag under that fitting over her head, so the crown falls to about the neck's value and the hairline and the bun read by their shapes and shadows. Check the window and wide frames at 1280: the back of the head must read as hair, with no spiral.

fixes.problem: The curtain wall barely reads as glass: no reflection of the lit pool or of Dawn, only two very faint ghosts of fittings. The floor also brightens toward the lens (about 38 at the glass, about 55 near the camera), which works against the silhouette.
fixes.fix: The curtain wall uses glass('window glass', refl=0.075) in departure_gate_mats.py. For the window camera only, raise that reflection to about 0.11-0.12 through a per-camera hook in apply_camera, as is done for the mast emission. The lit pool and her reflected face and front should then ghost faintly over the dark apron, at about 10-15 % of the apron's value. Keep visible_glossy off on the rim and face-return lights so no rectangles appear. Darken the near floor by trimming the DIMS fittings to about 0.4 in TRIMS['window'], or add a camera-invisible flag between them and the near carpet. Target the floor at the bottom centre under about 35 graded (now about 55), at or below the floor at the glass.

fixes.problem: The empty seat beside her (screen left, her right) is a large lit grey slab (about 62 graded in seated, 69 in seated_called) brighter than the rows behind it (38-43). It pulls the eye from Dawn, and its perforations risk moire on YouTube.
fixes.fix: flag_near_seats is a vertical plane at x of about 0.45 (SEAT[0] + 1.15). It shades only the seats beyond the next armrest, and the seat beside hers (centre x about -0.1) lies between the flag and the fitting. flag_pool should already cut the cone there, so first make a quick render with each light isolated to see which light lifts that seat: the overhead key, the seated face key or the window spill. Then flag that light off the seat, under FLAGS['seated'], which also covers seated_called. Target about 30-35 graded, with only its armrest catching an edge. Enlarge the perforation holes or soften their bump on that unit, or cut their contrast by about 30 %, so the dot grid does not alias at 1080p. A minor point for seated_called: a faint, lighter band of ceiling soffit runs along the top edge (x 270-470, y 0-14, about 27 against 20 below it). The 4 % push in 04-01 crops most of it by the end, but a slight tilt down would remove it.

fixes.problem: 8.9 % of graded pixels are below 8, the most in the stage. They sit in the corners: 27 % in the top left (the sky above the aircraft, part of the window that carries the place), 24 % in the bottom right and 20 % in the bottom left (the foreground seat rows).
fixes.fix: Leave the grade alone (A fixed). Lift the sky_dome and city_strip emission about 1.5x for the wide only. These are emission materials, not entries in st.LIGHTS, so TRIMS cannot reach them; set them per camera in apply_camera, the way the mast emission is set through _STATE['mast emission']. Add a faint cool area light behind the wide camera (about 8 W, spread 120) aimed at the foreground seat rows, so those seats separate at about 12-18 graded. Target under 5 % of pixels below 8 without lifting the frame median (now 23) above about 26.

fixes.problem: The airliner reads as a satin model. The fuselage has only a broad diffuse highlight along the upper left of the crown that rolls off to the nose side. No panel lines or door outlines read, and the wing is a flat-faced slab with square edges.
fixes.fix: In departure_gate_mats.fuselage, the faint panel lines and the 8 mm door grooves already exist. Deepen them (line value about 0.5 of the base) and add roughness variation of 0.25-0.45 with a Specular IOR Level of about 0.5, so the broad soft crown highlight tightens into a long specular streak from the masts. In departure_gate_aircraft.py the wing slab already tapers in thickness (0.5 / 0.22 m at the root, 0.14 / 0.06 m at the tip) but has planar faces and square edges. Give it an airfoil section: a rounded leading edge, by bevel or a lofted profile, and a trailing edge of about 3-4 cm. Optionally draw the covered carts' side curtains further back (cart() in departure_gate_set.py) so their bags and corner posts show and the carts stop reading as plain boxes.
